narrative.hero: Learning to sense the physical world
narrative.bio: I study how measurement physics can help learning systems perceive the physical world. My research connects optical measurement design with learned representations for image reconstruction and image-free perception. I am now exploring acquisition-aware learning and interfaces between optical signals and pretrained multimodal models. My long-term goal is sensing that lets AI systems and embodied robots genuinely understand the physical world.
narrative.direction: During my current visit at Politecnico di Milano, I plan to extend this work to time-domain diffuse optics and three-dimensional reconstruction, investigating how physical modeling can support transfer from simulation to optical experiments.
narrative.welcome: I welcome research collaborations and research internship opportunities in computational imaging, physics-aware machine learning, and multimodal sensing.
narrative.resume_summary: I work on optical measurement design and learning for imaging and perception. Current research explores acquisition-aware learning and pretrained models for optical signals.
narrative.long_term: Longer term, I want AI systems and embodied robots to understand the physical world through what they sense: learning from interaction, and choosing what to measure when it matters.
narrative.internship_summary: PhD student in computational imaging and physics-aware learning from optical measurements.
narrative.current_summary: Developing acquisition-aware models and adapting pretrained multimodal models to bucket-detector signals. Planned visiting research: time-domain diffuse optics and 3D reconstruction.

projects.title: The Lift Spectrum · Robust image-free perception
projects.summary: Without reconstruction, the hard part becomes the lift from 1D measurements to 2D features. Our STSF + TPLS lift keeps near-constant accuracy down to 0.78% sampling and, at 20 dB noise, beats clean-trained reconstruct-then-segment by up to 21.7 mIoU points.
bullets: Showed that removing reconstruction moves the design problem to the 1D-to-2D lift; organized lifts into a spectrum from fixed-physics inverse to content-adaptive retrieval.
Proposed STSF + TPLS: +3.2–9.9 pp mIoU over the prior image-free method, near-constant accuracy down to 0.78% sampling, and up to +21.7 pp over clean-trained reconstruct-then-segment at 20 dB noise.

projects.title: Sparse Hadamard single-pixel imaging
projects.summary: Gives orthogonal Hadamard patterns tunable sparsity: robust imaging through scattering and noise, high resolution from low-order matrices that save memory, and no training or post-processing.
bullets: Gave orthogonal Hadamard patterns tunable sparsity (two acquisition modes, full theory): noise-robust imaging through scattering, low-order matrices that save memory, and no training or post-processing.

projects.title: LDGI · Optical phased-array imaging
projects.summary: Line patterns from one-dimensional optical phased arrays break the noise symmetry that ghost-imaging denoising assumes; loop differential ghost imaging overcomes it, with orders-of-magnitude gains over traditional algorithms.
bullets: Showed that line patterns from one-dimensional optical phased arrays break the noise symmetry assumed by ghost-imaging denoising; proposed LDGI (orders-of-magnitude gains) and validated it optically.

projects.title: Acquisition-aware learning and multimodal measurement interfaces
projects.summary: Developing models that account for measurement conditions, and adapting pretrained multimodal models to bucket-detector signals.
bullets: Developing acquisition-aware models for reconstruction and perception across changing measurement budgets and acquisition conditions.
Adapting pretrained multimodal models to detector signals, with current work on fine-tuning for direct interpretation of bucket measurements.

directions.title: Learning with acquisition physics
directions.description: I am developing models that incorporate how signals are acquired, and studying how learned representations behave when acquisition conditions change.

directions.title: Connecting optical signals and pretrained models
directions.description: I am adapting pretrained multimodal models to bucket-detector signals, exploring how prior visual knowledge can support inference directly from measurements.

directions.title: Time-domain diffuse optics and 3D reconstruction
directions.description: During my current visit at Politecnico di Milano, I plan to investigate light-transport modeling and learning-based inversion for three-dimensional reconstruction.

platform_copy.linkedin_about:
I study how measurement physics can help learning systems perceive the physical world. My research includes noise-resilient Hadamard measurement design, ghost-imaging algorithms for optical phased arrays, and image-free segmentation. In The Lift Spectrum, our STSF + TPLS lift keeps near-constant accuracy down to 0.78% sampling and, at 20 dB noise, beats the strongest clean-trained reconstruct-then-segment baseline by up to 21.7 foreground-mIoU points.

I am currently exploring acquisition-aware learning and pretrained multimodal models for optical signals. My long-term goal is sensing that lets AI systems and embodied robots genuinely understand the physical world. I welcome research collaborations and internship opportunities in computational imaging, physics-aware machine learning, and multimodal sensing.
platform_copy.linkedin_about_zh:
我研究如何利用测量物理，帮助学习系统感知物理世界。已完成的工作包括抗噪的 Hadamard 测量设计、面向光学相控阵的鬼成像算法，以及免成像分割：在 The Lift Spectrum 中，我们的 STSF + TPLS 在采样率降至 0.78% 时精度几乎不变；在 20 dB 噪声下，前景 mIoU 比最强的干净数据训练先重建再分割基线高达 21.7 个百分点。

目前我在探索采集条件感知学习，以及面向光学信号的预训练多模态模型。长期目标是让 AI 系统与具身机器人通过感知真正理解物理世界。欢迎计算成像、物理驱动机器学习与多模态感知方向的科研合作与实习交流。
